title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
claim: Solution-processable rare-earth molecular emitters can reach near-unity exciton use in blue devices, and donor–acceptor surface ligands can supply the charge transport that insulating rare-earth nanocrystals otherwise lack.
explanation: An octahedral EutBu complex with tris(3-tert-butylpyrazolyl)borate is reported to use nearly 100% of excitons and to address low efficiency and poor stability of blue light-emitting devices. Carbazole–diphenylphosphine D–A ligands on nanocrystal surfaces speed intersystem crossing and carrier transport so the particles can be driven electrically despite an insulating core.
scope: Rare-earth molecular and nanocrystal optoelectronic emitters.
conditions: Octahedral pyrazolylborate Eu complex for the exciton-utilization claim; carbazole and diphenylphosphine surface functionalization for charge injection.
caveats: Device metrics other than the approximate exciton utilization are not extracted in the review text.
